text:
alex: Heads-up: eu-central GPU fleet failing periodic healthchecks after yesterday's stateful firewall tighten. Nodes mark Unhealthy and get ejected from balancer. Anyone oncall?

nina: saw increased node evictions + autoscaler churn this morning. Warm pool spin-ups exploded. cost alert fired (natgw bytes -> $2.3k extra/day). :grimacing:

ravi: symptoms = node -> keystore decrypt attempts succeed but control-plane /metrics POSTs timeout. packet traces show return path SNAT changed when stateful inspection is enabled on the border FW (inspection node rewrites src). healthchecks from control-plane come from original src but replies get NATed via different path -> TCP handshake fails.

alex: so it's *asymmetric routing* introduced by the new inspection route? that would break stateful sessions.

ravi: yup. firewall team enabled L7 inspection for auditshipper traffic to satisfy IDS rule IDS-2026-09. they also added a sticky SNAT pool but it is only sized for normal web traffic, not large-scale node churn.

security-bot: policy-note: IDS-2026-09 applied to subnet:eu-gpu-subnets at 2026-03-22T23:40:00Z by secops.

nina: consequence = many nodes retry join -> more NAT throughput -> NAT gateway autoscale -> cost. also control-plane marks nodes unhealthy because metrics POST never completes.

alex: mitigation options?

ravi: short-term options: 1) add specific stateful exception for keystore/control-plane healthcheck CIDRs so inspection bypasses SNAT; 2) route node egress via dedicated privatelink to avoid border inspection; 3) temporarily increase sticky SNAT pool size (if firewall supports).

nina: 1) fastest. but needs secops approval. 2) cleaner but infra-change-days. 3) might be quick if firewall team can bump pool. which gives lowest cost risk?

ravi: 1) best immediate cost reduction. it reduces callbacks going through NAT. 2) lowest long-term risk but will take 3-5 days. 3) medium.

alex: can we get secops to approve an emergency exception just for keystore (port 443) + control-plane health IPs? include expirations.

security-bot: secops triage: emergency exception requires owner sign-off + audit annotation. add justification and a 48h TTL preferred.

nina: I've drafted the exception request in the ticket INC-2026-1489. attaching minimal CIDRs and justification. pinging @secops.

ravi: quick snippet to validate in staging (iptables style) if you want to test bypass locally:
```
# allow egress to control-plane health IPs without conntrack rewrite
iptables -t raw -A PREROUTING -p tcp -s 10.0.0.0/16 -d 10.200.1.33 --dport 443 -j NOTRACK
```

alex: good. nina please include a perf check: expected NAT bytes drop, ejection rate drops to <1/hr, warm-pool scale-down to baseline within 30m. add runbook ID RB-2026-11.

nina: done. I also added cost calc: current extra NAT $2.3k/day, estimate exception reduces to ~$300/day. put numbers in ticket.

ops-bot: INC-2026-1489 created and labeled fw-urgent. mitigation=stateful-exception-request. Monitoring window 2h.

security-bot: secops approved emergency exception with 48h TTL (applied 2026-03-23T11:05Z). please instrument packet flows and report.

ravi: applied in staging and prod by fw-team. immediate improvement: nodes rejoined; ejection rate down to 0.2/hr. NAT bytes decreased by 78% in 15m.

alex: nice. next steps: 1) short retro with firewall and infra to design privatelink keystore path (long-term), 2) add conntrack health to our e2e checks, 3) update onboarding to mark control-plane health endpoints as inspection-exempt where safe.

nina: scheduling retro for tomorrow. i'll include cost tradeoffs, risk, and timeline for privatelink rollout.

ravi: also propose a policy: any L7 inspection toggle for subnets with high-churn compute needs must include a preflight test plan and conntrack sizing.

alex: agreed. closing loop after retro. thanks team. ping @oncall if anything regresses.
